ideas.title: SOQ Coach
ideas.person: A state-job applicant needs to answer a confusing Statement of Qualifications.
ideas.demo: Paste one sample posting and a fictional resume → draft an answer mapped to each prompt.
ideas.guardrail: Show missing evidence. Never invent qualifications.

ideas.title: Benefits Letter Decoder
ideas.person: A resident needs to understand a confusing benefits letter.
ideas.demo: Use a fictional letter → plain-language summary, next action, and highlighted deadline.
ideas.guardrail: Quote the source deadline; flag uncertainty and link to the issuing agency.

ideas.title: Scam Check Line
ideas.person: A neighbor wants a second opinion on a suspicious text.
ideas.demo: Paste a sample message → explain warning signs and offer a safe verification step.
ideas.guardrail: Say “possible scam,” not a guarantee. Never open suspicious links.

ideas.title: Heat & Smoke Check-In
ideas.person: An isolated resident needs a simple check-in during extreme weather.
ideas.demo: Simulate one opt-in call → ask how they are doing and show a sample resource.
ideas.guardrail: Use test contacts and labeled sample locations; no real emergency dispatch.

ideas.title: Skills Bridge
ideas.person: A worker wants to see how their experience transfers to a new role.
ideas.demo: Enter one occupation → show three adjacent roles and a short learning plan.
ideas.guardrail: Use example training data; verify availability before recommending enrollment.

ideas.title: Council Agenda, Plain English
ideas.person: A neighbor wants to know which local decisions affect them.
ideas.demo: Paste one agenda excerpt → summarize two relevant items and link to the source.
ideas.guardrail: Keep dates and public-comment instructions tied to the source.

ideas.title: SMS Resource Finder
ideas.person: A person with a basic phone needs nearby food or a shower.
ideas.demo: Use a text-message-style interface → search five sample resources by need.
ideas.guardrail: Label the dataset as demo data; show when hours were last checked.

ideas.title: AI at My Job
ideas.person: A workforce counselor needs a practical lesson for one occupation.
ideas.demo: Choose an occupation → generate one exercise, one example, and one limitation.
ideas.guardrail: Use fictional workplace information and include human review.

ideas.title: SacVoice
ideas.person: A resident wants to report a broken sidewalk, unsafe intersection, or illegal dumping in their preferred language.
ideas.demo: Record a voice message → translate and categorize it → confirm a mapped location → prepare a Sacramento 311 request draft.
ideas.guardrail: Let the resident review the translation and location. The prototype prepares a draft; it does not submit a report automatically.

ideas.title: LetterLens
ideas.person: Someone needs help understanding a government, school, utility, or housing letter.
ideas.demo: Upload a sample photo → explain it in simpler language → highlight deadlines and next steps → offer a translated version.
ideas.guardrail: Show the original wording alongside important dates. Use fictional letters and flag unclear text. Broader than the benefits-only decoder.

ideas.title: ReadySac
ideas.person: A family wants to practice making decisions during floods, wildfires, smoke events, or extreme heat.
ideas.demo: Try a five-minute practice scenario → make interactive choices → receive a preparedness checklist based on those choices.
ideas.guardrail: Clearly label scenarios as practice. Use official guidance; this is not a live alert or emergency response service.

ideas.title: StoryPins
ideas.person: Residents want to preserve and share Sacramento neighborhood history through their own audio stories.
ideas.demo: Record a short story → create a transcript and translation → choose a map pin → play the neighborhood story.
ideas.guardrail: Get permission before publishing a recording. Let contributors review transcripts and choose an approximate public location.
